mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a slowdown in corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of periods when HOUST and RSAFS both decline.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), supply constraints lead to higher inflation and potential Fed tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: A strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0%) signals robust economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of periods when GDPC1 > 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading above 5.0% (CPIAUCSL > 5.0) indicates persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to accelerate rate hikes, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 5.0.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of weak payroll growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.2% MoM) and rising unemployment (UNRATE > previous month) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which typically leads to lower consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth < 0.2% and UNRATE rises.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market downturn (HOUST < 1200), the broader economy is affected due to the housing sector's role in the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of periods when HOUST < 1200.
